      "id": "Q1",
      "category": "K1",
      "question": "How will the user consume the helpers on real exports, and is any entry point beyond the module export required?",
      "changes": "The consumer-facing entry point and end-to-end verification.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use the existing CommonJS module entry point in src/text.js; do not add a CLI or deployment.",
      "blocks": "Discovery of existing consumers and export formats precedes the entry-point decision; otherwise nothing: the default proceeds."
    },

      "id": "Q2",
      "category": "K2",
      "question": "What did the old trim helper do, and are there existing consumers or compatibility requirements outside the visible files?",
      "changes": "The record helper's scope and preserved behavior.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Preserve all current squash string behavior and expose a separate record helper; do not invent unrelated compatibility behavior.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must first look for the old helper and consumers in available repository history or workspace sources; otherwise the recorded default proceeds."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q3",
      "category": "K3",
      "question": "What name and exact input, output, and error contract should the record-wide helper use?",
      "changes": "The exported API and its contract tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Export squashRecord from src/text.js; accept a plain record and return a new record with each own enumerable string-keyed field passed through squash, propagating TypeError for invalid field values.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must first establish the old helper's public contract and representative export shape; if unavailable, the recorded default proceeds."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q4",
      "category": "K4",
      "question": "How should empty records, nullish fields, invalid field types, arrays, nested values, inherited properties, and symbol keys behave?",
      "changes": "Boundary rules and edge-case tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Apply squash to each own enumerable string-keyed field of a plain record; nullish fields become empty strings, invalid field values throw TypeError, and unsupported record shapes are rejected. Do not recursively traverse values or process inherited or symbol keys.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must first check the old helper and real export shape; if unavailable, the recorded default proceeds."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q5",
      "category": "K5",
      "question": "Did the old helper mutate its input or preserve special property characteristics, and do consumers depend on that?",
      "changes": "Record ownership, mutation behavior, and compatibility tests.",
      "route": "inspect",

      "blocks": "Discovery must first inspect the old helper and consumers; if unavailable, the recorded default proceeds."
    },

      "id": "Q6",
      "category": "K6",

      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use the existing dependency-free CommonJS and node:test setup; add no dependency or runtime configuration.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must first inspect available project configuration and runtime; if no version policy is found, the recorded default proceeds."

      "id": "Q7",

      "changes": "Where the new function lives and how it is independently exercised.",
      "route": "inspect",

      "blocks": "Discovery must first inspect repository structure and the old helper; if no other seam is found, nothing: the default proceeds."
    },

      "id": "Q8",
      "category": "K8",
      "question": "Which boundary checks and existing test conventions establish the scalar and record contracts?",
      "changes": "The test cases and verification command.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use node:test and node:assert through npm test, covering the exported functions, existing string behavior, nullish values, invalid types, and record edge cases.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must first inspect the test suite and settle the record contract; otherwise nothing: the default proceeds."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q9",
      "category": "K9",
      "question": "Does dogfooding require a delivery target or access beyond returning the updated source checkout?",
      "changes": "The delivery step and any required access.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Deliver the usable module and tests in the returned source checkout; no release or external access is assumed.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must first look for an existing delivery target or consumer instruction; if none is found, nothing: the default proceeds."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q10",
      "category": "K10",
      "question": "Is there an existing performance budget or representative workload for one million records?",
      "changes": "The performance acceptance check and any optimization decision.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use a straightforward readable implementation and avoid speculative optimization; do not invent a latency or memory threshold.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must first look for a stated budget and representative data; if absent, nothing: the default proceeds."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q11",
      "category": "K11",
      "question": "Are the named code-review and improve skills available to the delivery run, and can they examine the resulting changes in the requested order?",
      "changes": "The required review and improvement workflow and its verification.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use the host-listed code-review skill for edge cases, then run improve on its findings; record any unavailable skill as an unresolved delivery requirement.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must first verify the installed skills and their instructions; their respective review steps cannot be completed if unavailable."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q12",
      "category": "K12",
      "question": "Where is the Orchard doc-comment style guide, and what rules apply to these helpers?",
      "changes": "Doc-comment wording and style verification.",
      "route": "research",
      "default": "Keep comments consistent with the existing concise style provisionally; do not claim Orchard compliance without the guide.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must first locate the guide in authorized workspace or internal documentation; final Orchard compliance remains open and needs an owner or guide if discovery fails."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q13",
      "category": "K12",
      "question": "Does 'usual whitespace' mean the current JavaScript trim and regular-expression whitespace behavior?",
      "changes": "The accepted whitespace set and regression tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Preserve the existing trim() and /\\s+/g behavior exactly for strings, including its JavaScript-defined whitespace set.",

  "summary": "S1 fact: The work concerns the small Node.js text-record helper repository; this intake is read-only and implements nothing. S2 fact: squash must return an empty string for null and undefined and continue throwing TypeError for numbers and objects, with other non-string types retaining their existing rejection. S3 fact and assumption: Add a separately exported record-wide helper modeled on the old trim helper; Q2–Q5 route discovery of its name, field and mutation contract, with recorded defaults if evidence is unavailable. S4 fact and assumption: Make the returned module usable for the user's real-export trial tomorrow; discover existing consumers and export shapes without assuming access to real data or adding a new delivery target. S5 fact: Use an installed review skill, with code-review acceptable, to examine edge cases, then run improve on its findings; Q11 verifies availability and instructions before those steps. S6 fact: Keep regular expressions readable in one pass. S7 fact and assumption: Preserve the current JavaScript whitespace behavior for strings; Q13 records the interpretation. S8 fact: Follow the Orchard doc-comment style guide; Q12 directs discovery to authorized team or workspace documentation and leaves compliance open if the guide cannot be found. S9 fact: Preserve squash's current string results exactly, including trim() and /\\s+/g behavior. S10 fact: Add tests in the existing node:test and node:assert style and run npm test. S11 fact and assumption: Support practical use at one million records with straightforward code and no speculative optimization; Q10 seeks a representative workload or stated budget without inventing one. Discovery source hints, not verified facts: repository history or workspace for the old trim helper and consumers; team channels, internal sites or docs, private repositories, and owners for Orchard, export formats, runtime policy, performance expectations, and skill instructions; no sensitive locator was supplied, and any discovered sensitive locator belongs only in an authorized private store, never KNOWLEDGE/. The named source checkout is the delivery target and grant; an isolated run's source checkout remains at its snapshot until final return, when the changed module and tests become visible there. No deployed outcome exists unless a later release is authorized and completed. This is a library request, not an interactive product: no actor identification, cross-session shared state, session lifetime, hidden state, or product runtime is requested."
